source.title: Coherent Gradients: An Approach to Understanding Generalization in Gradient Descent-based Optimization

record.file_problem: none; full conference paper text supplied
record.tranche_reason: Tests memorization and held-out generalization on MNIST, and changes label noise and gradient updates to examine generalization.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports training and validation curves for clean and noisy labels; the text says all five variants reach 100% training accuracy and have different generalization. Figure 4 reports training, validation, and overfit curves for winsorized SGD. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study repeats the natural-label versus random-label training comparison in a new setting: fully connected MNIST networks trained with vanilla SGD without explicit regularization. Its own results directly bear on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose coherent per-example gradients as a mechanism favoring updates that benefit many examples, and present MNIST label-noise and winsorization experiments as supporting evidence. They offer heuristic arguments rather than a formal or broadly validated explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses vanilla SGD and a fully connected MNIST network, but tests label-noise levels and gradient winsorization rather than the cited Zhang et al. architectures and datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: Training label noise changes validation generalization; winsorization level changes the overfit curve and can impair training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing coordinate-wise gradient winsorization slows overfit growth, but stronger winsorization impairs fitting and can make training and test accuracy decline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing extreme per-example gradient contributions can reduce overfitting on MNIST, with a training-fit cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Pristine examples are learned faster than corrupt examples, and sampled gradient statistics suggest different contributions to loss reduction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient coherence and learning dynamics differ between correctly labeled and corrupted examples.

record.problems: The main curves are figure-only without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The gradient-contribution analysis samples 400 per-example gradients for 600 weights; the paper says the null comparisons are somewhat significant but not overwhelming and suggests using the full population in future work.
record.rows_left_out: Winsorization results in Figure 4 are not tabulated as separate rows; the text gives qualitative trends but no condition-specific numeric values. Figure 2 and Figure 3 gradient-contribution statistics are not mapped to the listed versions.

untested.parts: The named CIFAR-10 and ImageNet architectures and recipes are not tested. Chance-level held-out accuracy after fully randomized training cannot be independently verified from the supplied figure text.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width required for interpolation; the proposed explanation for wider networks is future work.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison with specified matched epoch budgets; the qualitative full-batch observation does not establish this comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking against norm and margin measures.
No removal and retraining experiment using memorization-ranked examples.

missing.what: The authors report that replacing minibatch SGD with full-batch training produces similar qualitative generalization results. Extract this as a qualitative V1 result, retaining the lack of numerical endpoints and training-budget details.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. The supplied figure extraction preserves axes and legends but not readable curves, so condition-specific numerical accuracies should not be reconstructed. Winsorization and gradient-statistic results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a one-hidden-layer fully connected MNIST network, not the named Inception, AlexNet, MLP CIFAR-10, or ImageNet settings.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold was not varied.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures.
